title: Adaptive brand token fallbacks and component overrides for deep-dark console themes
creator: Jules O'Neill
description:
Problem: When customers apply custom brand palettes to the Redwood Console in deep/dark mode, several components degrade: low-contrast buttons, unreadable table row separators, and chart axis/gridlines that disappear against dark backgrounds. Existing token mapping assumes light-first brand palettes and relies on simple invert/fade heuristics that don't hold for high-saturation or low-luminance brand colors.

Goal: Produce a robust, deterministic mapping and per-component override strategy so any brand palette produces accessible and visually consistent dark-mode output without requiring engineering to craft manual themes for each customer. This ticket scopes the design work and the token-level rules; engineering ENG-4120 will implement the runtime mapping layer and a migration path for existing themes.

Scope: semantic token rules for background/foreground, emphasis, borders, dividers, chart primitives, and state (hover/active/disabled); component override guidelines for Button, Table, DataGrid, and Chart components; design artifacts and acceptance criteria for QA and automated visual tests.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Theme adapter defines deterministic fallback rules so brand palettes with primary luminance < 30% generate adjusted semantic tokens that meet WCAG AA for normal text against the chosen surface.
2) Buttons (primary/secondary/ghost) must maintain >=3:1 contrast for icon+text in default state and >=4.5:1 for text when labeled as critical actions.
3) Table row striping and dividers remain visible at 14px/400 weight text and with selected-row states.
4) Charts: axis, gridlines, and small-multiple outlines are legible; at least two accessible palette options auto-generated from brand palette for chart series.
5) Design handoff includes token mapping docs, SCSS/CSS var examples, and three example brand themes (low-luma, high-saturation, desaturated) with screenshots and Percy tests references.
proposed_solution: Introduce a 'brand-adapter' token layer that ingests customer brand tokens (brand-50..brand-900 or a custom primary/secondary/neutrals set) and outputs semantic tokens used by the component library. The adapter will: 1) compute perceptual L* (LAB) of key brand swatches and decide a dark-mode transform (lift, desaturate, or swap to neutral range); 2) provide explicit overrides for 'interactive' tokens (button-bg, button-text, control-border) using contrast-first heuristics; 3) export a small set of chart-safe series derived from the brand using hue-preserving desaturation. Provide component override guidance for Button (shadow/outline removal in dark), Table (divider thickness and alpha adjustments), and Chart (axis stroke weight + anti-aliased color choices). Deliver a design token spec and 3 high-fidelity theme mockups in Figma, plus a lightweight 'theme-lab' preview file for engineering to consume.
implementation_tasks: Design: finalize token mapping matrix and 3 example brand themes (Aisha)
Design: produce Figma components + redline annotations for Button/Table/Chart overrides
Design: create visual regression test cases and Percy snapshots
Engineering: implement brand-adapter (ENG-4120) and add token hooks into component library
Engineering: add runtime preference toggle (auto-adapt | prefer-custom) and migration guide
Product: validate with two enterprise customers (PM-303) for brand fidelity and compliance
test_plan: Visual regression snapshots for: baseline Redwood brand, low-luma brand, saturated neon brand, desaturated brand. Automated contrast checks for all semantic token pairs referenced by components. Manual QA checklist for Buttons (hover/active/focus), Tables (selected rows + compact density), Charts (palette legibility at 16px axis labels). Include accessibility audit steps with VoiceOver/JAWS for focus states in dark themes.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: land design tokens and adapter feature flag behind 'theming-v2' in console-2026.03. Phase 2: enable for new brand uploads by default, provide a 'preview' toggle in theme editor. Phase 3: migrate existing customer themes gradually with email notices and opt-out. Coordinate with Customer Success before mass migration.
follow_up: Post-launch: monitor support tickets tagged 'theme-fidelity' for 30 days
Collect telemetry on theme-adapter decisions to refine heuristics
Consider authoring an 'advanced brand editor' for enterprise customers who need pixel-perfect control
